edges.description: Neutrophil enzyme release damages the vessel wall.
Damaged vessel walls permit erythrocyte leakage, while the inflammatory infiltrate makes purpura palpable.
Leukocytoclastic injury occurs in small cutaneous vessels.
Neutrophilic vessel-wall injury with nuclear fragmentation is the leukocytoclastic histopathologic pattern.
More severe cutaneous vascular injury can progress to ulceration.
A culprit drug supplies the antigen around which immune complexes form, which is why withdrawal is the primary treatment. The intermediate is antibody generation against the drug or its metabolite.
Preceding infection or vaccination supplies a foreign antigen by a different route than drugs but feeds the same immune-complex step.

A paraneoplastic association in a small minority of cases. Whether tumour antigen drives complex formation directly is not established here, so this is recorded as a predisposing context rather than an antigen source.
